what_was_wired: B10 (occupancy) and B11 (RevPAR) for a pinned annual period

why_these_two_now.they_were_the_only_pair_whose_open_side_: eight metrics have a trait gate and only the closed side was answered. Six are gated on `financial` and the one company whose traits open that gate has no reachable period, so there is nothing to write an open side against. B10 and B11 are gated on `lodging` and the one hotel in this repository holds three saved annual originals.
why_these_two_now.and_the_ordinary_route_is_deterministic: `lodging_table_source` rebuilds the whole table set and matches the scope contract against the table's own headers and geometry. No model call, so wiring it needs no allowance.

what_was_measured_before_writing_it.method: ask the ordinary chain the same question first

the_one_rule_replaced: `prepare_saved_lodging_source` calls `prepare_saved_annual_input`, which means the newest annual report. Everything downstream already takes the filing and the period as arguments - `inspect_lodging_table_source` re-derives the source's own annual period from its bytes and refuses if it disagrees - so pointing it at a pinned filing is a substitution, not a reimplementation.
an_independent_corroboration: the FY2023 figures agree with what the table-qualification work read out of the same filing by a different route and recorded in AGENTS.md - RevPAR 124.70 and Occupancy 69.2 - which was measured for a different purpose and is not this route's own output.

counting_changed_too.what: STRUCTURAL_APPLICABILITY_METRICS is now derived by subtracting the wired set rather than listed
counting_changed_too.why: the two families are added to count the metrics that have a route, and B10 and B11 now have one on both sides of the gate. Leaving them in both would count them twice; subtraction also means the next metric to gain an open side leaves the tuple by itself.
counting_changed_too.dispatch_unchanged: `historical_structural_results`'s own supported set still carries them, so a company that is not a hotel still gets the structural answer.

what_this_does_not_do.five_years: B10 and B11 read only the target filing - no prior period, no accession index - so they are the cheapest historical metrics in the set, but a period whose primary document is not saved still produces a named source gap. Three of Marriott's five target years have their original; two do not.
what_this_does_not_do.other_companies: none. Eight of the ten are not hotels and the ninth, JPMorgan, is a bank whose period selection refuses on incoherent saved history.
what_this_does_not_do.content_acceptance: not claimed. The values agree with the ordinary route and with an independent reading of the FY2023 filing; neither is a business acceptance of the figures.
